keyVerseText: In his days did Hiel the Bethelite build Jericho: he laid the foundation thereof in Abiram his firstborn, and set up the gates thereof in his youngest son Segub, according to the word of the LORD, which he spake by Joshua the son of Nun.
rootMeaning: The name חִיאֵל (Chîyʼêl) is derived from the Hebrew roots חַי (chay), meaning 'alive' or 'living,' and אֵל (El), meaning 'God.' Together, the name literally means 'God lives' or 'living of God.' This etymology emphasizes the concept of divine life or the living presence of God, which enriches the common English gloss by highlighting a vibrant, ongoing relationship with God rather than a static title.
usageInScripture: The word חִיאֵל appears only once in Scripture, specifically in 1 Kings 16:34, where it is translated as 'did Hiel.' This consistent translation as a proper name reveals its function primarily as an identifier of a historical figure rather than a common noun. The singular occurrence underscores the uniqueness of Hiel as the Bethelite who undertook the rebuilding of Jericho.
theologicalSignificance: The name חִיאֵל, meaning 'God lives,' carries profound theological weight by affirming God's enduring life and presence even in the midst of human actions and failures. The figure of Hiel, associated with the rebuilding of Jericho, reminds believers that God's living word and covenantal promises remain active and authoritative. This name invites reflection on the tension between human obedience and divine judgment, illustrating that God's life is sovereign over history and human endeavors. For the Christian faith, it points to the living God revealed in Christ, who sustains all things and calls His people to faithful obedience.
keyVerseReflection: In 1 Kings 16:34, 'In his days did Hiel the Bethelite build Jericho: he laid the foundation thereof in Abiram his firstborn, and set up the gates thereof in his youngest son Segub, according to the word of the LORD, which he spake by Joshua the son of Nun,' the name Hiel anchors the narrative in a personal history of disobedience and fulfillment of divine judgment. The meaning 'God lives' contrasts with Hiel's tragic actions, underscoring the seriousness of God's living word spoken through Joshua. This verse highlights the reality that God's life and authority persist even when human beings attempt to defy His commands.
